questions.q: A plano-convex lens has curved-surface radius 20 cm and refractive index 1.5 in air. Using the lens-maker relation, what focal length does it have and does reversing the lens change its converging nature?
options: A) f = +40 cm, and it remains converging whichever side faces the object.
B) f = +10 cm, but it is converging only from the curved side.
C) f = -40 cm, so it is diverging from either side.
D) f = +20 cm, and reversing it makes it diverging.
questions.answer: A) f = +40 cm, and it remains converging whichever side faces the object.
questions.explanation: For a plano-convex thin lens in air, one surface has infinite radius and the other has magnitude 20 cm. The lens-maker relation gives 1/f = (1.5 - 1)(1/20), so f = 40 cm with positive sign for a converging lens. Reversing a thin lens changes the order of the surfaces but not its focal length in the same surrounding medium.

questions.q: For the same glass lens, is the focal length for red light greater than, equal to, or less than that for blue light?
options: A) Smaller, because red light has larger refractive index.
B) Greater, because glass generally has a smaller refractive index for red than for blue, reducing optical power.
C) Equal, because focal length depends only on surface curvature.
D) It alternates with object distance.
questions.answer: B) Greater, because glass generally has a smaller refractive index for red than for blue, reducing optical power.
questions.explanation: The optical power of a lens in air is proportional to n - 1 for fixed radii. In normal dispersion, the refractive index for blue light is greater than for red light. Therefore blue light is focused more strongly and has a shorter focal length, so the red focal length is greater.

questions.q: An object approaches a converging lens from the left with constant speed and stops at the first focal point. How does the real image move as the object approaches the focus from beyond it?
options: A) Toward the lens with constant speed.
B) Away from the lens with constant speed.
C) Away from the lens with non-uniform acceleration, receding to infinity as the object reaches the focus.
D) Toward the lens with uniform acceleration.
questions.answer: C) Away from the lens with non-uniform acceleration, receding to infinity as the object reaches the focus.
questions.explanation: For a converging lens, 1/f = 1/v - 1/u under the usual sign convention, so as the object distance approaches the focal distance from beyond, the image distance grows without bound. The relation between v and u is nonlinear, so constant object speed does not produce constant image speed. The image therefore moves away with non-uniform acceleration and tends to infinity at the focus.

questions.q: An astronomical refracting telescope has objective focal length 20 m and eyepiece focal length 2 cm, adjusted for normal viewing. Which set of statements is correct?
options: A) Tube length is about 19.98 m and magnification is 100.
B) Tube length is about 20.02 m but magnification is 10.
C) Magnification is 1000 but the final image is erect.
D) Tube length is about 20.02 m, angular magnification magnitude is 1000, and the image is inverted.
questions.answer: D) Tube length is about 20.02 m, angular magnification magnitude is 1000, and the image is inverted.
questions.explanation: For normal adjustment, telescope length is fo + fe = 20 m + 0.02 m = 20.02 m. The angular magnification magnitude is fo/fe = 20/0.02 = 1000. A simple astronomical refracting telescope produces an inverted final image, so all three features in option D are consistent.
